newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's top court delays phone rate ruling.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's top court delays phone rate ruling.

text.p: A Supreme Court ruling on rate changes by Argentina's two telephone companies has been postponed because of unrelated accusations against one of the high court's judges, a court spokesman said Tuesday.
The court was expected to announce a ruling Tuesday on an overhaul in rate structures which Telefonica and Telecom tried to carry out following authorization by a presidential decree in late January.

But a decision has been postponed until after the courts' two-week winter break starting next week because its nine members had it had to deal instead Tuesday with charges against one of them, Supreme Court Judge Carlos Fayt.

Members of Argentina's Jewish community want Fayt removed over investigations into the bombing of the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires in 1992, which killed 29 people. They question whether he can be impartial given his statement that an extremist Jewish group might have placed the bomb.
"There was no resolution (on phone rates) because they had to deal with the objection to Fayt," said the spokesman.
Fayt has not publicly responded to the questions raised by representatives of the Jewish community.

Telefonica and Telecom's tariff changes, which pushed up local rates but made big cuts in long-distance calls, sparked conflicting court actions which must be resolved by the Supreme Court. Both companies got into trouble with the courts for not billing their clients while awaiting the ruling.
